question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the edge of the road (to the right),b:Turn them away from the edge of the road (to the left),c:Keep them straight
note: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge so the vehicle will roll off the road if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it required to signal when changing lanes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must use the appropriate turn signal to indicate intent to change lanes so others can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does ''yield'' also require you to stop if you cannot merge safely into traffic?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If you must yield and cannot safely merge into the flow of traffic, you must stop and wait for a safe gap.

question: The statement 'Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane and should be passed like other vehicles' is:
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcyclists may use the entire lane and drivers should pass them the same way as any other vehicle, allowing a full lane of space.

question: You are being tailgated. What should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Maintain the same distance as usual,b:Increase the space ahead of your vehicle,c:Decrease your following distance
note: If another driver is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking to reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, you should:
options: a:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing,c:Pass as slowly as possible
note: When passing, do so quickly and safely and return to your lane only when you can see the other vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers,b:Drink coffee and continue,c:Open a window and keep driving
note: The safest option when tired is to stop and rest or have another licensed driver take over.

question: When weather or low visibility requires lights, which should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:High beam headlights,c:Parking lights
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain because high beams can reflect and create glare, reducing visibility.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts,c:Use only the lap belt
note: Using both lap and shoulder belts together provides the intended protection; using only one part greatly reduces safety.

question: At a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed,b:Slow down, look and listen for trains,c:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly
note: Where there are no active warning devices, slow, look both ways, and listen for approaching trains before crossing.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change as a vehicle's speed increases?
options: a:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,c:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: Higher speeds result in longer stopping distances and more severe crashes; increase following distance as speed rises.

question: A vehicle with a bad suspension can cause which problem?
options: a:Squealing brakes,b:Vehicle control problems,c:Slack in the steering
note: Worn suspension components can reduce vehicle control and make the ride unsafe; have them repaired.

question: For quick and controlled turns, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel for better control, especially at higher speeds.

question: When your traffic signal turns green while waiting at an intersection, should you still look before proceeding?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Even on green, check left and right for vehicles or pedestrians that may still be in the intersection before proceeding.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads, what should you do?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Slow down.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: Reduce speed when roads are wet to lessen the risk of hydroplaning; avoid sudden steering inputs and heavy braking.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction
note: When a broken yellow line is beside a solid yellow line, traffic next to the broken line may pass while traffic next to the solid line may not.

question: If you are on a highway next to a single broken white line, are you allowed to cross it?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass,b:You may cross to pass or change lanes,c:You may only cross it from the left lane
note: A dashed white line allows lane changes and passing when it is safe to do so.

question: What is the penalty for illegally passing a stopped school bus in Illinois?
options: a:Driving privilege or vehicle registration suspension and a mandatory $300 fine,b:A 60-day suspension of driving privileges,c:A $30 fine and 14-day suspension
note: Passing a stopped school bus with red lights and stop arm extended carries a mandatory $300 fine and suspension of license or vehicle registration.

question: If you are involved in or come upon a traffic crash, should you stop in a safe, well-lit public place that does not obstruct traffic if able?
options: a:True,b:False
note: If involved in or coming upon a crash, stop in a safe, well-lit public place that does not obstruct traffic, help injured persons, call 911, and exchange information.

question: Which best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They expect no breaks and give none.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They assume other drivers will do the right thing.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and stay prepared to respond safely.

question: When a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is crossing, must you yield to them?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians who use a guide dog or white cane must always be yielded to; they have the right-of-way.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Squeeze between the large vehicle and the curb to turn,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn,c:Turn quickly before the truck or bus finishes its turn
note: Large vehicles need extra space to complete turns; wait until they finish before you turn to avoid collisions.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down help,b:Sound your horn at passing cars,c:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible
note: If you must stop on the interstate, pull off the road, activate hazard lights, and remain in the vehicle if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful when passing?
options: a:Passing in any marked no-passing zone,b:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing,c:Both of the above
note: You may not pass in marked no-passing zones or over railroad crossings; both actions are illegal and unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should slow vehicles stay in the left-hand lane except when passing?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Slow vehicles should use the right-hand lane except when passing or turning left.

question: Must headlights be on from sunset to sunrise?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when is the correct time to reduce speed?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then reduce speed to the advisory speed posted for the exit ramp.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly than traffic for 200 feet,b:Wait for a large enough gap to accelerate to traffic speed,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then merge
note: Only merge when there is a gap large enough for your vehicle to accelerate to the speed of traffic.

question: Does Illinois law require headlights to be on when windshield wipers are in use?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Illinois law requires headlights to be used whenever windshield wipers are needed due to weather or visibility conditions.

question: Under low-visibility conditions caused by fog, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beams,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights,c:Increase your speed to clear the area quickly
note: Slow down and use low beams in fog; if visibility is severely limited, pull off the road and wait.

question: Is it true that cellphone use while driving is permitted if the driver is over 18 and using hands-free?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Illinois prohibits handheld cellphone use and texting while driving. Hands-free devices are allowed only for persons age 19 and older.

question: What should you do about following distance when driving at night?
options: a:Always use high beams,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights,c:Increase your following distance
note: Reduced visibility at night means you should increase following distance to allow more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right,b:Passing cars,c:No one
note: Drivers making a left turn must yield to all vehicles approaching from the opposite direction, including bicycles and motorcycles.

question: Can driving privileges be revoked for giving false information to the Secretary of State?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Submitting false information on a driver license application can result in arrest, imprisonment, or suspension/revocation of driving privileges.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you,b:Only when slowing down,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot
note: Check your rearview mirrors frequently to keep track of the positions of vehicles near you and maintain situational awareness.

question: As daylight fades, which lighting should you use to help other drivers see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:Parking lights,c:Emergency flashers
note: When daylight begins to fade, turn on your low beam headlights to help others see you. Use high beams only when no other drivers are present.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Use low beam headlights or fog lights in foggy conditions; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: To restore driving privileges after losing them for failure to pay crash damages, what must a driver do?
options: a:Nothing specific is required,b:File proof of financial responsibility with the Secretary of State,c:Pay a small fine to the court
note: Drivers who caused damage and have no insurance must post proof of financial responsibility to reinstate privileges.

question: Will your driving privileges be suspended if convicted of illegally passing a stopped school bus?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A conviction for passing a stopped school bus with flashing lights and stop arm extended will result in license suspension; owners must identify drivers or face registration suspension.

question: Is the road surface of a bridge likely to remain icy longer than the rest of the roadway in winter?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Bridges and overpasses can remain icy when the rest of the road is clear because they cool more quickly from both top and bottom.

question: If a law enforcement officer stops your vehicle, should you exit immediately and approach the officer’s squad car?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If stopped by law enforcement, remain in your vehicle with both hands visible (usually on the steering wheel) until the officer instructs otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you entered an intersection on a green light to make a left turn but the signal then turns red, how should you complete the maneuver?
options: a:Make sure it is clear, then back up from the intersection.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and complete the left turn.,c:Wait in the intersection until the light turns green.
note: If you entered the intersection on a green, you may complete the left turn when it is safe, yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: On a freeway why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards early,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic
note: On the freeway you must watch far ahead to spot hazards and be ready for rapid changes in traffic conditions.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, how should you respond?
options: a:Drive around the gates if you don't see a train,b:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are raised,c:Slow and carefully drive around the gates
note: You must stop and remain behind lowered gates with flashing lights; it is illegal and dangerous to drive around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Must drivers yield to pedestrians in an unmarked crosswalk?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A driver must yield to a pedestrian in an unmarked crosswalk on the driver’s side of the roadway when there are no traffic control signals.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, may they use the left lane?
options: a:Yes, they may use the left lane,b:No, they must wait on the side of the road,c:They may cut through all lanes
note: Expect bicyclists to ride with traffic and to use the left lane when making left turns.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road,b:Switch to high beams,c:Turn your lights on and off repeatedly
note: If oncoming headlights blind you, glance toward the right edge of the road (not directly ahead) until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic and pedestrians?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
note: Drivers making left turns must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight and to any pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: Should a railroad crossbuck sign be treated like a yield sign?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A crossbuck indicates you must yield the right-of-way to trains and railroad equipment; proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it lawful to make a right turn on red after stopping and yielding when not prohibited?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You may turn right on red after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and traffic unless a sign forbids it.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic indicates what?
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe,b:Both lanes of traffic are going the same direction,c:Passing is not permitted
note: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; vehicles may pass when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

question: Are taillights required to be illuminated after dark?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and vehicles must have two red taillights visible from 500 feet to the rear (one for motorcycles/mopeds).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, does the vehicle that arrives first have the right-of-way?
options: a:False,b:True
note: At an all-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you; proceed in turn when it is your right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you reduce speed below the posted limit?
options: a:Both when driving in unfavorable weather conditions and when approaching/crossing an intersection,b:Only when approaching and crossing an intersection,c:Only when driving in unfavorable weather conditions
note: Weather and traffic conditions may require driving slower than the posted limit. Slow down when approaching intersections, curves, hills, or narrow roads.

question: Is it illegal to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Illinois law requires headlights be used when driving after dark; using only parking lights at night is unlawful.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it required to set the parking brake?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Set the parking brake and turn on emergency flashers to alert other drivers when stopped on the roadside.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind,b:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost,c:It draws the attention of other drivers
note: Using a cell phone while driving distracts the driver by engaging hands, eyes, and attention, increasing crash risk.

question: What is typically the first skill affected by alcohol use?
options: a:Balance,b:Judgment,c:Vision
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, which leads to reduced driving skills.

question: If you are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on your right, should you yield to the bicyclist?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Allow the bicyclist to go through the intersection before you turn; yield to them as appropriate to avoid cutting them off.

question: Approaching an octagonal traffic sign requires you to:
options: a:Turn.,b:Stop.,c:Slow.
note: An octagonal sign always means STOP: come to a complete stop, yield to others, and go when it is safe.

question: Can a parent or guardian cancel a minor's driver license any time before the minor turns 18?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A parent or legal guardian who gave a minor permission for a license may request cancellation at any time before the minor reaches 18.

question: If weather or darkness reduces visibility, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Speed up to leave the area sooner.
note: Increase following distance to allow more time to detect and react to hazards when visibility is poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb,b:When pulling next to but not away from the curb,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb
note: Signal both when you are pulling toward a curb and when you are pulling away so other road users know your intentions.

question: Is it ever safe to stop on railroad tracks even for a short time when moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never stop or park on railroad tracks; only cross when there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side of the tracks.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, should occupants still use seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are supplemental protection and should be used in combination with lap and shoulder belts for maximum safety.

question: A traffic sign with an orange background generally indicates what?
options: a:Regulatory requirement,b:Warning in a construction or maintenance area,c:A scenic route ahead
note: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance; drivers should be alert and reduce speed accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check blind spots,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane
note: Do not make sudden lane changes. Check mirrors and blind spots and signal to allow others time to react.

question: Drowsiness, like alcohol or drugs, can do what to your driving?
options: a:Make you a safer driver,b:Improve alertness,c:Impair your judgment
note: Lack of sleep slows reaction time and impairs judgment similarly to alcohol and drugs.

question: Is alcohol the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Alcohol is a leading factor in fatal crashes because it impairs vision, reaction time, and judgment even at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds,b:When you cannot see the vehicle over your right shoulder,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
note: You may return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror; always signal before changing lanes.

question: The three-second rule is useful for determining a safe following distance.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Use the three-second rule in normal driving conditions to estimate a safe following distance behind the vehicle ahead.

question: Which actions should you take before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:All of the above (signal, check mirrors and blind spots).,c:Check your blind spots and mirrors.
note: Always signal your intent, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes or passing.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver makes a mistake,b:Only to help prevent a collision,c:Whenever another vehicle is in your way
note: Use your horn to warn others of danger or to help avoid collisions; do not use it aggressively.

question: How far before meeting another vehicle must you dim your high beams?
options: a:250 feet,b:400 feet,c:500 feet
note: Dim high beams at least 500 feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle to avoid impairing the other driver's vision.

question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and to pedestrians crossing the driver’s side in unmarked crosswalks when required.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces your time to react and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to pass on a two-lane two-way roadway within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is unlawful to pass within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing on a two-lane two-way road.

question: A "No passing zone" sign communicates which message to drivers?
options: a:Increase speed slightly,b:It is not safe to pass,c:Maintain a steady speed
note: A 'No passing zone' sign indicates that passing in that area is illegal and unsafe due to limited visibility or other hazards.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights (regardless of direction or road type)?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When approaching a school bus that is using its flashing red lights, you must stop before you reach the bus and remain stopped until the flashing lights are turned off. On a two-way multilane roadway with a median or shared center lane, vehicles on the opposite side of the road from the school bus do not have to stop.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, where should you look?
options: a:Look straight ahead.,b:Look toward the right edge of the road.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.
note: Look toward the right side or edge of the road to avoid being blinded and to maintain enough view of the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light when you approach it?
options: a:You are traveling in the wrong direction,b:Treat it like a stop sign and stop before proceeding,c:Wait until it changes to green before moving
note: A flashing red signal means stop. Come to a full stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when safe,b:Slow and proceed with caution,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light is green
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop like a stop sign; yield to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

question: Which substances can impair driving ability?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving; check labels and warnings before driving.

question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what is the safest immediate action?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and continue,b:Slow, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway,c:Turn on high beams and proceed with caution
note: If smoke limits visibility, slow down, pull off the road to the right, stop, and assess conditions before continuing.

question: If arrested with a BAC of 0.08% or more, will your driving privileges be suspended for at least six months?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A chemical test showing a BAC of 0.08% or higher results in a six-month suspension of driving privileges.

question: Which situation listed may lead to suspension of driving privileges?
options: a:The individual is over 21 and convicted of illegally transporting alcohol twice within 12 months,b:Three reckless driving offenses in 12 months,c:Drag or street racing
note: If you are over 21, your license may be suspended for one year if you are twice convicted within a one-year period of illegally transporting alcohol; other serious offenses can also lead to suspension.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance,b:Be ready to use your horn,c:Drive more slowly than usual
note: When following a motorcyclist, allow at least a three- to four-second following distance so the rider has space to maneuver and stop safely.

question: What message appears on a red, octagonal traffic sign?
options: a:One-way,b:Do not enter,c:Stop
note: An eight-sided (octagon) sign always means 'STOP' and requires a complete stop at the sign.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn up the radio to stay awake,b:Increase your speed to finish sooner,c:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap or rest
note: Fatigue impairs driving; stop in a safe location to rest or switch drivers if possible.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving
note: Driving above posted limits or too fast for conditions commonly contributes to crashes. Drive with the flow of traffic within legal limits.

question: When there is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Vehicles in the lane next to the broken line may pass,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane indicates you may pass when safe; a solid yellow next to you means you may not pass.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, which of the following should you NOT do?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: Do not pump the brakes. Instead, hold the wheel steady, ease off the accelerator, and brake lightly when safe to do so.

question: Traffic control devices like cones, drums, and signs in a work zone are used to:
options: a:Annoy drivers,b:Inconvenience drivers,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work areas
note: Work-zone devices direct traffic and protect both workers and motorists by marking hazardous areas.

question: If an overhead sign shows an arrow with the word "ONLY" beneath it, what must you do?
options: a:Travel in the direction of the arrow,b:Always make a lane change,c:Look for a destination sign to follow
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and "ONLY" means you must proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow.

question: Which driving technique is recommended during inclement weather?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: Use smooth steering and gradual braking to maintain control in bad weather; avoid sudden maneuvers.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control while driving on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You should not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads because tires may lose traction and you can lose control of the vehicle.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee,b:Wait and allow time to pass,c:Take a cold shower
note: Only time removes alcohol from the body; coffee or showers do not speed up alcohol elimination.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, the best course is to:
options: a:Open a window and continue,b:Drink caffeine and keep driving,c:Stop and get rest or change drivers
note: Stopping to rest or changing drivers is the safest response to drowsiness; caffeine or open windows are temporary measures.

question: To obtain court supervision for a traffic violation, must a minor appear in court with a parent and attend traffic safety school?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Minors seeking court supervision must appear with a parent or guardian and attend a traffic safety program as ordered by the court.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, how should you act?
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them,b:Expect the child to be fully in control,c:Expect the unexpected
note: Children can be unpredictable; anticipate sudden movements and give extra space.

question: On an undivided road, when a school bus is loading or unloading children with red lights flashing, must you stop regardless of your direction of travel?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.,c:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
note: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, no matter your direction of travel, unless separated by a median as defined by law.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.,b:If you are under the legal BAC limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and decision-making needed for safe driving; impairment can occur even below legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately enter and speed to match traffic,b:Use the shoulder to get up to speed,c:Speed up only after identifying a safe gap in traffic
note: On short entrance ramps without acceleration lanes, wait for a safe gap and then accelerate to merge smoothly into traffic.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow enough to be able to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible
note: Drive slowly at night so you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, what should you do first?
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic,b:Press down hard on the accelerator,c:Set the parking brake
note: Before stopping, check mirrors and be aware of surrounding traffic as you ease off the accelerator and apply the brake smoothly.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, how should you respond?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,c:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop; watch for workers, equipment, and lane changes as you enter a work zone.

question: If you become stranded in a blizzard, should you stay with your vehicle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Stay with your vehicle; run the engine only periodically for heat, crack a window for ventilation, and conserve fuel and battery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal for anyone to wear a dual-ear headset while driving?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Illinois prohibits the use of headsets that impair hearing except for hearing aids; a single earpiece is allowed for phone use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,c:Merge carefully into the gap when it is safe.
note: Accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge carefully into an adequate gap without assuming other drivers will yield.

question: If a pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane, what must you do?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:Honk your horn to alert them.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians have the right-of-way; yield and exercise caution when they are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers slow to the posted school zone speed?
options: a:On school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs posted,b:Only on weekends,c:Only during recess
note: Reduce speed to the posted school zone limit (often 20 mph) on school days during posted hours when children are present.

question: Do you need to allow as much following distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; you should allow at least a three- to four-second following distance when behind a motorcycle.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what is the safest action?
options: a:Challenge them to a race,b:Get out of their way,c:Speed up to avoid them
note: Do not engage; safely move out of the aggressive driver's path or let them pass to avoid escalation.

question: Is it illegal for drivers under 21 to have any detectable alcohol or drugs in their system while driving?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers under 21 are subject to zero-tolerance laws; any detectable alcohol or controlled substances can result in license suspension and penalties.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams and they blind you, where should you look?
options: a:Look to the left edge of your lane,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane,c:Look straight ahead into the lights
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming high beams; glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to monitor the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing yellow traffic light, you should:
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing,b:Stop, then enter the intersection only when it is clear,c:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to stop unless required by traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Left-turning drivers must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:No one,b:Oncoming vehicles,c:Vehicles overtaking on the right
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight through the intersection.

question: If driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights to improve visibility?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, use low beams or fog lights; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it safe to move back into the right lane only when you can see the entire passed vehicle (or its headlights) in your rearview mirror?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not return to your lane until the entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.

question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone while driving significantly increase crash risk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Using a phone while driving is a distraction and significantly increases the risk of being involved in a crash.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving,b:Whenever you need to use them while moving,c:Before you get into the car
note: Adjust mirrors before moving the vehicle as part of your pre-driving checks for safety.

question: Which road surface is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A road in a shaded area,b:A residential road,c:A hilly open road
note: Shaded spots often freeze before and thaw after the rest of the roadway, making them more likely to be icy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but see no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: If no gap is available, slow on the ramp to find a safe space to enter; do not stop at the end of the ramp where you cannot accelerate to road speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To which pedestrians must you give the right-of-way?
options: a:Only those in marked crosswalks,b:Those in any crosswalk or intersection,c:Only pedestrians crossing at signalized intersections
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and generally yield to people crossing the street for safety.

question: Is it illegal to drink from or possess an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle on a highway?
options: a:True,b:False
note: It is illegal for drivers or passengers to possess an open container of alcohol in a motor vehicle while it is in operation.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Continue; you have the right-of-way,b:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing,c:Drive around them by pulling to the right
note: Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and wait until they have crossed safely before proceeding.

question: Must a motor vehicle's horn be audible from 200 feet away?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Every vehicle must have a horn that can be heard from 200 feet; sirens and bells are reserved for emergency vehicles.

question: Which behavior describes defensive driving?
options: a:Keeping your eyes fixed on the car directly ahead,b:Putting one car length between you and the vehicle ahead,c:Keeping your eyes moving to scan for hazards
note: Defensive driving means scanning ahead, checking mirrors, and constantly assessing potential hazards rather than staring at one spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley, building, private road, or driveway in an urban area, must a driver come to a complete stop before entering the roadway?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must stop and yield to roadway traffic and pedestrians when emerging from alleys, driveways, or private roads.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly,b:Pump the brakes,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to stop
note: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) require firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal; the ABS will pump the brakes automatically.

question: Are most rear-end collisions caused by the vehicle in back following too closely?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Following too closely is a leading cause of rear-end crashes; maintain a safe following distance.

question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be driving?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway,b:Five to ten mph slower than freeway traffic,c:At the posted speed limit regardless of traffic
note: When merging you should accelerate to enter at or near the speed of traffic to merge safely.

question: Slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual event on the roadway typically:
options: a:Helps traffic flow,b:Prevents rear-end collisions,c:Causes traffic congestion
note: 'Rubbernecking' slows traffic and increases the risk of collisions as drivers divert attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you are one vehicle length ahead,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,c:When you are 50 feet ahead
note: Only return to your lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic,b:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up,c:Always maintain your position
note: When traffic permits, make room to allow vehicles to merge into your lane to improve safety and traffic flow.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait for the owner to return.,b:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: Leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the damaged vehicle or property, and report the crash if required.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles
note: When faced with oncoming traffic on one side and parked cars on the other, steer a middle course between them to reduce collision risk.

question: Signs with an orange background are used for what purpose?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warnings,b:Regulatory messages,c:General warning signs
note: The color orange is used for construction and maintenance warning signs.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Four-way flashers
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: When a train is approaching, vehicles must stop within what distance of the nearest rail?
options: a:Within 15 to 50 feet,b:Within 5 to 10 feet,c:Within 10 feet
note: At railroad crossings you must stop within 15 to 50 feet of the nearest rail when signals or gates indicate a train is approaching.

question: Blue highway signs typically provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services (like rest areas, food, hospitals),b:Construction and maintenance,c:Mileage to destinations
note: Blue signs are service signs providing information about motorist services such as rest areas, food, or hospitals.

question: May only vehicles displaying special plates or placards for persons with disabilities park in spaces reserved by an official sign?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Only vehicles with valid disabled plates, disabled veteran plates, or disabled parking placards may use spaces reserved for persons with disabilities.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, which lights should you use to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Turn on your parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Increase instrument panel lighting.
note: Use your headlights when visibility is reduced. In rain, use low beam headlights when windshield wipers are required.

question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane and skid on water, should the driver immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not slam on brakes during hydroplaning; release the accelerator and steer straight until traction returns.

question: Is driving allowed while under the influence of any medication that impairs your ability?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:If it is prescribed by a physician,c:If you do not feel drowsy
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal drugs—that impairs your ability to drive safely.

question: Are you required to obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:Only during school hours,b:At all times,c:Only if children are visible
note: Drivers must obey crossing guards and their directions whenever they are performing their duties.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed,b:Drive at the posted speed,c:Speed up
note: Slow down in wet, snowy, or icy conditions because tires have less traction on slippery surfaces.

question: What are “No zones” around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into the truck's blind spots or are so close they limit the truck's ability to stop and maneuver,b:Areas with several car lengths between vehicles and the truck,c:Spaces safe to travel behind the truck
note: “No zones” are areas around trucks where cars can be in blind spots or so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop or maneuver safely, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: Orange construction signs indicate what kind of area ahead?
options: a:Roadwork or construction ahead,b:You must change lanes ahead,c:There is a detour ahead
note: Orange-colored signs indicate construction or maintenance areas; proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Activate your turn signal,b:Reduce your speed,c:Brake hard while in the curve
note: Slow down before you enter a curve to maintain control; avoid hard braking while turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection,c:Turn left and find another route
note: Do not enter an intersection if the way ahead is blocked even when you have a green light; remain out until traffic clears.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Press hard on the brake pedal,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking suddenly,c:Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times
note: Hold the steering steady, ease off the accelerator, and allow the vehicle to slow before carefully pulling off the road; avoid hard braking.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should drivers be especially alert for?
options: a:Watch for multiple trains.,b:Both of the above (vehicles that must stop and multiple trains).,c:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, hazardous-material trucks).
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution: watch for trains and for vehicles required to stop at crossings, and only cross when safe.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol level can result in license suspension?
options: a:Any amount,b:0.08 percent or more,c:0.15 percent or more
note: Illinois enforces zero-tolerance for under-21 drivers; any detectable amount of alcohol can result in penalties including license suspension.

question: Reaction time is slower after which action?
options: a:Drinking alcohol,b:Sleeping,c:Working hard
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, making driving more dangerous.

question: What do diamond-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:Warning,b:Stop,c:Yield
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special conditions or hazards ahead and are typically yellow (or orange in work zones) with black markings.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way,b:A slow-moving vehicle,c:Shoulder work ahead
note: An orange-red triangle marks slow-moving vehicles like farm equipment or maintenance vehicles.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Maintain a steady speed and allow the pass.,c:Brake hard.
note: Yield to the passing vehicle and do not increase your speed so it can safely merge back into the lane.

question: After stopping for a train and it passes, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait for all signal lights to stop flashing and watch for a second train,b:Proceed immediately as soon as the first train passes,c:Ignore signals if you do not see another train
note: After a train passes, check for a second train and do not proceed until all gates are raised and all warning signals have stopped.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approach, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it passes,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes
note: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed, positioning parallel to the curb if possible.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must you do regardless of your direction of travel?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.,c:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
note: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, no matter your direction of travel, unless separated by a median as defined by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only when which condition is present?
options: a:Traffic on the street you are turning onto is moving to the left,b:You increase your speed before turning,c:Traffic on the street moves to the right
note: You may make a left turn from one one-way street onto another only if traffic on the street you are entering moves to the left and no sign prohibits the turn.

question: When driving through a work zone, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop,b:Increase your speed to get through quickly,c:Maintain your normal speed
note: When entering and driving through a work zone, slow down, obey posted speed limits, and be alert to changing conditions and workers present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder of the road?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Passing on the shoulder is not permitted; remain on the traveled portion of the roadway when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn must you signal continuously in a business or residential district?
options: a:Not less than 100 feet before turning,b:Not less than 50 feet before turning,c:Not less than 75 feet before turning
note: In business or residential areas you must give a continuous turn signal at least 100 feet before turning (200 feet in other areas).

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend far behind the vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Large vehicles can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large trucks because the driver may not see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing, what should you check?
options: a:Beep your horn,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,c:Flash your headlights
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: Must a crash report be filed by the driver regardless of fault if the crash involves death, injury, or property damage over a specified amount?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A report must be filed if a crash involves death, bodily injury, or property damage over $1,500; if any vehicle is uninsured, the threshold is $500.

question: At a red light with a green arrow displayed for your lane, when may you proceed in that arrow's direction?
options: a:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear,b:Only after the red light changes,c:Only after coming to a complete stop first
note: If you are in a lane controlled by a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates:
options: a:Do not pass,b:Reduce your speed,c:Traffic light ahead
note: A solid yellow line next to the center indicates passing is prohibited from your lane.

question: If a pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane while crossing, must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Pedestrians who are blind or partially blind using a guide dog or white cane have the right-of-way and you must yield to them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not working?
options: a:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.,b:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,c:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering.
note: If signals are inoperative, treat the intersection as an all-way stop: stop, then yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles also turning left,b:All approaching vehicles,c:Pedestrians waiting at the crosswalk for a "Walk" signal
note: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and oncoming traffic that have the right-of-way.

question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:
options: a:Merging into a different lane when possible,b:Maintaining your speed and position,c:Never changing lanes
note: If possible, merge into the adjacent lane to create a gap; if you cannot, adjust your speed to allow entering vehicles to merge safely.

question: Temporary construction and maintenance signs have which color scheme?
options: a:Orange background with black writing,b:Red background with green writing,c:Yellow background with blue writing
note: Temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black symbols and text.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws,c:Only if traffic signals favor the pedestrian
note: You must take all reasonable actions to avoid striking pedestrians and yield to them as necessary for safety.

question: At about what speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:35 miles per hour,b:45 miles per hour,c:40 miles per hour
note: Hydroplaning can occur on standing water. At speeds up to about 35 mph, most tires will channel water away; above that, tires may lose contact with the road and begin to hydroplane.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights,b:Use high beams,c:Use low beam headlights
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: If your tires feel like they've lost contact with the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,c:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: Ease off the accelerator, avoid braking or turning abruptly, and wait until traction returns before making adjustments.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while on the highway helps to:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning,b:Allow you to spot police officers,c:Help you keep up with traffic
note: Watching far ahead on the highway allows you to anticipate changes and avoid last-minute maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stop sign that has no marked crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Before entering the intersection,b:At the center of the intersection,c:Only if pedestrians are present
note: At an unmarked stop sign you must stop before entering the intersection; if there is a stop line or crosswalk, stop at that location.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, what should you try to do with the vehicle?
options: a:Stop in the right travel lane,b:Park with all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the road if possible,c:Stop where you are and leave hazards on
note: If possible, move your vehicle completely off the traveled portion of the road to a safe location.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Enter partially to establish right-of-way,b:Do not enter until you can get completely across,c:Proceed into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking the intersection is illegal and unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline prohibits passing; passing is allowed only when the broken line is nearest your lane.

question: Does refusing a chemical test after arrest result in a three-month suspension of driving privileges?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Refusal to submit to chemical testing generally results in a one-year suspension of driving privileges (six months for drivers under 21).

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently,b:Using high beams in fog,c:Staring at the road directly ahead
note: To remain aware of hazards, scan the road and check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds. Use low beams (not high beams) in fog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed because you have the right-of-way,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians,c:Pedestrians must wait for you to pass
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection even when their signal is green.

question: A large truck turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction may:
options: a:Have to swing wide to complete the right turn,b:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning,c:Complete the turn in either lane
note: Long vehicles often swing wide to make right turns because the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: The statement 'A teen driver may carry only two passengers under age 20 during their first 12 months of licensing' is:
options: a:True,b:False
note: For initial licensing (ages 16-17), the limit is one passenger under age 20 for the first 12 months, except for siblings or children.

question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain you should:
options: a:Slow down,b:Drive at speeds appropriate for ideal conditions,c:Apply brakes as soon as your car starts to skid
note: To prevent hydroplaning, reduce speed in wet conditions so tires can maintain contact with the road.

question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Pull to the left-hand edge of the roadway and stop,c:Pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass
note: Drivers must pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus on a two-lane roadway with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, must you stop?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must stop before overtaking a school bus that is loading or unloading passengers on a two-lane road until the stop arm is retracted and lights turn off.

question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control,b:Pump the brakes,c:Apply the brakes lightly
note: If the vehicle begins to skid, avoid braking; correct your steering until control is regained.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Be aware of everything happening around your vehicle.
note: Maintain a constant scan of the front, sides, and rear to detect hazards early and respond appropriately.

question: Can you use only parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must use headlights when visibility is reduced after sunset; parking lights alone are not lawful for night driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow center lines to pass another vehicle when which condition is met?
options: a:The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.,b:The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,c:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
note: You may cross double yellow lines to pass only when the broken line is on your side and it is safe to pass.

question: After a train clears a crossing with flashing signals, when may drivers proceed?
options: a:As soon as the train passes on the nearest track,b:After the lights stop flashing and you have visually checked for a second train,c:When the gate rises even if lights are still flashing
note: Proceed only after lights stop flashing, gates are up, and you have checked all tracks for additional trains.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is actively leading them across the street,b:At all times,c:Only if a crossing guard is present
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian enters after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing and is mid-street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed since you have the green,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane,c:Wait until the pedestrian has cleared the street before moving
note: Yield to any pedestrians already in the intersection; wait until they finish crossing before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another car?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:If the other vehicle is turning left,c:If the shoulder is wide enough
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; the other driver will not expect a vehicle there and it creates a hazardous situation.

question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02% has what effect on crash risk?
options: a:It has no effect on driving.,b:It doubles your chances of having an accident.,c:It does not put other drivers at risk.
note: Even low levels of alcohol (0.02% BAC) significantly increase the risk of a crash; impairment begins well below legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, from which lane should you begin the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb,b:Any lane as long as it's safe,c:The center lane
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, begin the turn from the far-left lane.

question: If your front right wheel runs off the pavement, how should you re-enter the road?
options: a:Brake hard and steer sharply back onto pavement,b:Ease off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow, then gently steer back on,c:Rapidly accelerate to regain control
note: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, allow the vehicle to slow, check traffic, then gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: If a traffic signal displays a red light and a green arrow, is it true that you may not turn in the arrow's direction until the red light changes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A green arrow allows you to make the indicated movement after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, even if other signals are red.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid left, how should you steer to correct it?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left toward the skid.,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right away from the skid.,c:Keep your hands off the wheel and do not turn.
note: When a vehicle skids, steer in the direction of the skid and ease off the accelerator; if equipped with ABS, apply brakes firmly while steering straight if recommended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder,b:Attempt to pass or change lanes while in an intersection,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane
note: Never change lanes or pass in an intersection; check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: When a school bus ahead has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.,b:Drive around the bus cautiously.,c:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: You must stop and remain stopped until the bus’s red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted, then proceed only when safe.

question: If your license was revoked for DUI, must you meet specific requirements to get it back?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Reinstating a revoked license for DUI typically requires alcohol/drug evaluation, education or treatment, hearings, and payment of a reinstatement fee.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians even if they walk against the traffic signal?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians; they may misjudge signals so be prepared to yield.

question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least what percent?
options: a:0.05 percent,b:0.08 percent,c:0.02 percent
note: For drivers age 21 and over, the legal blood alcohol concentration limit is 0.08% or higher for DUI enforcement.

question: If a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children
note: Vehicles must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and stop arm extended until the signals are turned off and the bus moves.

question: Which statement is true about large trucks?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly
note: Large trucks require significantly more distance to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed.

question: Which driving abilities are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness,b:Coordination,c:Both alertness and coordination
note: Substance use impairs multiple driving skills including coordination, alertness, reaction time, and concentration.

question: Even a small amount of alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's:
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination,b:Right-of-way privileges,c:Knowledge
note: Any alcohol can impair judgment and coordination; even low BAC levels may affect driving ability.

question: When is it necessary to use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street,b:On a freeway,c:In fog
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or mist to avoid glare from high beams reflecting off moisture.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Because they lack adult reflexes,b:Because they are smaller and harder to see,c:Both of the above
note: Children are often unpredictable and harder to see; give them extra space and caution.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Pull over quickly.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brake and hold it.
note: Grip the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, and brake lightly until you can safely pull off the road.

question: How does higher vehicle speed affect stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,b:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,c:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
note: Stopping distance grows and collisions become more severe as vehicle speed increases; increase following distance at higher speeds.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection instructs drivers to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Stop immediately,c:Stop and proceed only when intersection is clear
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to come to a complete stop.

question: When passing a line of parked cars, what should you expect?
options: a:That every pedestrian and driver will yield to you,b:That someone or a vehicle may unexpectedly enter your lane,c:That you can drive close to parked cars to make more room for traffic
note: Leave space when passing parked vehicles; people and vehicles can unexpectedly enter traffic from between parked cars.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road,c:Keep your wheels straight
note: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn left toward the center of the road,b:Turn right toward the edge of the road,c:Keep the wheels straight
note: When parked facing downhill on a road with no curb, turn the wheels toward the side of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: A curb painted red indicates what restriction?
options: a:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,b:No parking, standing, or stopping.,c:Loading zone.
note: Red-painted curbs mean no stopping, standing, or parking at any time unless otherwise posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking your mirrors, what should you do?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots,b:Always slow down in your lane,c:Never look over your right shoulder
note: Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to ensure there is no vehicle in the lane you intend to enter.

question: May drivers open car doors on the traffic side only when it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A driver or passenger may not open a vehicle door on the side where traffic is moving unless it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates what?
options: a:Stop sign,b:Regulatory sign,c:School zone or school crossing sign
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign warns of a school zone or school crossing where children may be present.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are small and easy to miss, what should drivers do?
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:Make frequent visual checks for smaller vehicles.,c:Always slow down near them.
note: Constantly scan for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds; they can be hidden in blind spots or overlooked in quick glances.

question: When approaching a construction area, what should motorists do?
options: a:Increase speed to pass quickly,b:Slow down, stop wireless phone use, and yield the right-of-way,c:Honk repeatedly to alert workers
note: Illinois law requires motorists to slow down, avoid handheld phone use, yield to workers and authorized vehicles, and proceed with caution in construction zones.

question: If a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph,b:Stop until the lights stop flashing,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously
note: You must stop for a school bus that has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended; remain stopped until the signals are turned off.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding,c:Yield to pedestrians only
note: A green arrow permits the movement but you must first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and go when safe.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does a "Merging lanes" sign mean drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A "Merging lanes" sign indicates two lanes will soon become one; be prepared to merge or let others merge.

question: If you have a tire blowout, should you apply the brakes quickly and then pull off the road?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If experiencing a blowout, ease off the gas, hold the steering wheel firmly, and steer to safety. Do not brake suddenly.

question: How long must vehicles remain stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing?
options: a:Until all students are off the bus,b:Until the stop arm is retracted,c:Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion
note: Motorists must remain stopped until the bus's red lights are off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to make a left turn at a red light from a one-way street onto another one-way street that goes left?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You may turn left on red from one one-way street onto another one-way street where traffic moves left, after a complete stop and yielding.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles,b:You must yield to pedestrians,c:Construction workers must yield to drivers
note: Pedestrians in a crosswalk have the right-of-way and drivers must yield to them unless directed otherwise by a traffic control device.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping
note: At a yield sign you must slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard.

question: If you are involved in a minor intersection crash with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave it where it is in the travel lane until police arrive,b:Move the vehicle out of the traffic lane if safely possible,c:Never move the vehicle for any reason
note: If no one is injured and it's safe, move vehicles out of traffic to reduce the risk of additional collisions.

question: Is it legal for a driver to use a hands-free device while driving unless they are under age 19?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Illinois law allows hands-free devices for persons age 19 and older; handheld use and texting while driving are prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you ever enter an intersection if doing so will leave you blocking it when the light turns red?
options: a:Enter only if you got into the intersection on a green light.,b:Do not enter under any circumstances.,c:Enter only if you entered on a yellow light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely before the light turns red; blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to drive through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green,b:Follow the officer's directions and proceed without stopping,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding
note: Officers directing traffic override traffic signals. Follow their instructions even if lights indicate otherwise.

question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You must stay in your lane at all times,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes,c:You may only change lanes from the left lane
note: A broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and allows lane changes when safe.
