question: When following another vehicle at night, should you dim your headlights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You should dim your headlights when following vehicles at night (including motorcycles and trucks) to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed,b:Slow down,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain
note: Hydroplaning is caused by high speeds on wet pavement; slow down to reduce the risk.

question: How must you yield to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop,b:Stop immediately even if you are in an intersection,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by driving as closely as possible to the right edge of the road and stopping, taking care not to stop in an intersection. Resume driving after it has passed.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is generally:
options: a:Appropriate in all conditions,b:Good if you don’t know the posted speed,c:Often a hazard because it may cause others to pass dangerously
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause frustration and risky passing maneuvers by other drivers.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure about your vehicle position?
options: a:Share the lane with the motorcycle since it is small,b:Blow your horn so the rider moves over,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a lane; when passing, use a full lane and do not crowd the rider.

question: How should you behave when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers,b:Decrease following distance,c:Pass carefully and do not slow down to ''rubberneck''
note: Drive cautiously through work zones, maintain safe spacing, and do not slow down merely to look at the activity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow centerline means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear,b:Passing is not permitted,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: At a school crossing sign (five-sided), what should drivers do?
options: a:Always stop regardless of conditions,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop,c:Always sound the horn when children are present
note: A pentagonal sign warns of a school zone or crossing; be alert and prepared to stop for children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Only where signs and pavement markings allow passing.,c:Within an intersection if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: Only pass where signs and pavement markings allow and when you have enough clear space and visibility to do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a steady yellow traffic light and have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Come to a safe stop,b:Speed up to beat the red light,c:Reduce speed and proceed through the intersection
note: If you see a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, prepare to stop safely rather than speed up.

question: To reduce the risk of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections,b:Speed up to enter a curve and slow to exit it,c:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill
note: Slow down before entering curves because you cannot see what is ahead; braking on a curve may cause a skid.

question: When following a truck at night, should you dim your headlights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Dim your headlights to avoid glare in the truck driver’s mirrors; bright lights can reflect and reduce their visibility.
